conviction_note: Each finding sized on its own sums to about +0.4: a likely beat on a disputed $2.0m revenue bar, a reaffirmed FY guide and a crowded short roughly cancel a going-concern, covenant-bound balance sheet with dilution resuming. The scaled number is -2.1 (p_up 42, abs 13) because this name fell after 6 of its last 7 prints, including after a revenue beat (Q1: $0.94m vs $0.20m, -21%), and it raised equity a week after its last print. The gap between the two numbers is the reaction function overruling the fundamental read; it is not an inconsistency.
bar: Q3 2026 revenue consensus $2.00m, EPS -$0.75 (MarketBeat, https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/MVIS/earnings/). Investing.com shows a ~$2.5m revenue forecast without naming the quarter, so there are not two agreeing sources and every revenue finding is capped small. The company's own bar is the FY2026 revenue guide of $10-15m, reaffirmed 2026-10-07 after Q3 had closed (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65770/000149315226046140/ex99-1.htm), against H1 revenue of $2.41m (10-Q), so H2 has to be $7.6-12.6m. A $2.0m Q3 would leave Q4 needing $5.6-10.6m, so the street consensus looks low against the guide or is assuming the guide fails. print_vs_bar_pct of +40 means about $2.8m Q3 revenue against $2.0m, an inference from the guide and the August IRIS orders.
positioning_check: Short interest: 6.2M shares at the 2026-09-30 FINRA settlement, 4.3 days to cover (Curved Trading, via search snippet, https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/mvis/short-interest/; the page itself returned 403). That is about 20% of the ~30.15M shares outstanding after the August offering (13G of 2026-09-18, https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65770/000205845126000002/xslSCHEDULE_13G_X02/primary_doc.xml). MarketBeat shows 30.4% of float, 3.83 days, up 15% month on month, undated (https://www.marketbeat.com/stocks/NASDAQ/MVIS/short-interest/). Borrow fee is listed as 27.4% (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/mvis/). So the short is crowded. No skew: the front-expiry chain (2026-10-30) is unusable, with no two-sided ATM quotes; put/call OI is 0.77 on 607 contracts in total. The tape is 93% off its 52-week high and 8.9% above its 52-week low, -18% over 20 days. It fell 21% on 2026-10-07 to 10-09 on about 8.7M shares after the business update, and is +2.5% over 5 days.

findings.finding: Q3 revenue is likely above the $2.0m consensus. On 2026-08-24 MicroVision announced purchase orders for 'thousands' of IRIS sensors from new and repeat customers in North America and Europe, with inventory available now. The Q2 call said the semiconductor engineering project (15% of Q2 revenue) would add more revenue in Q3 as it completes. The FY $10-15m guide was reaffirmed after Q3 closed, which implies H2 revenue of $7.6-12.6m against H1's $2.41m. Q2 revenue was $1.47m against a $1.0m estimate.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: Revenue beats have not paid. Q1 2026 revenue was $0.94m vs $0.20m est. and the stock fell 21.05%; Q2 was $1.47m vs $1.0m and it rose 3.99%. Misses were punished: Q4 2025 was $0.22m vs $3.0m and the stock fell 29.49%. Sources: MarketBeat earnings table and the baseline.
findings.why_not_priced: The street bar of $2.0m is barely above Q2's $1.47m. If the market believed the guide's H2 ramp, the consensus would sit nearer $3-5m and the stock would not trade at about the value of its cash. The order release gave no dollar value, so no estimate could be built off it. Capped small because the bar has one source.
findings.independence: Q2 call summary on semiconductor revenue in Q3: https://www.nasdaq.com/articles/microvision-q2-earnings-call-highlights (via search snippet). The FY guide reaffirmation in the 2026-10-07 8-K (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65770/000149315226046140/ex99-1.htm) is shared with the guidance finding.

findings.finding: The FY2026 revenue guide of $10-15m and the projection that 2027 revenue doubles were reaffirmed in an 8-K on 2026-10-07, after Q3 had closed. That makes a guide cut at this print less likely. The market did not believe it: the stock fell from $1.52 to $1.20 over the next two sessions on about 8.7M shares.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The guide has been held at $10-15m all year (Q4 2025 through Q2 2026) while H1 delivered only $2.41m. The Oct 7 reaffirmation was followed by -21% over two sessions. A cut would most likely be repriced like the Q4 2025 revenue miss (-29.5%).
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. The -21% after Oct 7 shows the market treats the guide as unlikely. A third reaffirmation backed by a Q3 number that is plausibly on the path would be a small relief against that disbelief. If the market believed the guide, the stock would not have fallen on the reaffirmation. The risk on the other side is real: Q4 would need a 2-4x sequential step.
findings.independence: Shares the 2026-10-07 8-K with the reported-quarter finding. The stock's move after that 8-K comes from the Yahoo daily bars (https://query1.finance.yahoo.com/v8/finance/chart/MVIS?range=3mo&interval=1d).

findings.finding: The balance sheet is the negative. The 10-Q carries 'substantial doubt' going-concern language. The senior secured zero-coupon convertible note had $25.6m outstanding after July conversions; the holder can demand $3.0m plus a 10% premium every month, with $19.8m scheduled for the rest of 2026, and there is a minimum-cash covenant of the lesser of $17.5m or 110% of the note. FY burn is guided at about $60m (H1 operating cash use was $35.6m). The ~$15.6m net raised on 2026-08-14 (6.8M units at $2.50, now 51% underwater) came with a 45-day ban on note repayments and new issuance that lapsed around 2026-10-01. The Oct 7 update gave no cash figure and said the company is 'evaluating ways to strengthen its balance sheet' (debt structure, leases, non-core asset sales). Rough Q3-end cash is ~$28-30m against a $17.5m floor, so a restructuring, ATM use or a new raise announced with the print or the night after is likely.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The last raise (announced 2026-08-13, a week after the Q2 print) took the stock from $3.77 to $2.24 in a day (-41%) and to $1.80 within three sessions. The Oct 7 balance-sheet language was followed by -21%.
findings.why_not_priced: Partly priced. Market cap is about $37m against ~$28m of cash and a $25.6m senior note, so equity holders are already pricing near-zero net cash. What is not yet visible is the Q3-end cash number, the use of the ATM since Oct 1, and the form of any debt restructuring. On the 'what does the money buy' question: it funds survival and a 2027 burn reduction, and the only demand evidence is undated, unpriced POs, so it is not a corroborated ramp. Shrunk from a larger negative because of the ~20% short and 27% borrow.
findings.independence: The 424B5 of 2026-08-14 documents the 45-day repayment and issuance restriction (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000065770/000149315226038620/form424b5.htm). The 2026-10-07 8-K's 'evaluating ways to strengthen the balance sheet' is shared with the guidance finding (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65770/000149315226046140/ex99-1.htm).

findings.finding: The short is crowded: about 6.2M shares short at the 2026-09-30 settlement (~20% of ~30.15M shares outstanding; MarketBeat shows 30.4% of float), 4.3 days to cover, and borrow listed at 27.4%. With daily turnover of only ~$1-2m, any positive surprise (a revenue beat, a held guide, a non-dilutive debt fix) has a squeeze mechanism.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: No clean prior squeeze on a print in the baseline. The only up print (Q2, +3.99%) came on a revenue beat with short interest rising.
findings.why_not_priced: Positioning is a mechanism rather than information. It makes the right tail fat and does not move the expected price before the print. If the short had already covered, short interest would be falling and borrow would be cheap; both point the other way.
findings.independence: Curved Trading: 6.2M short at 2026-09-30, 4.3 days, borrow 27.4% (https://curvedtrading.com/stocks/mvis/, search snippet only).

findings.finding: Operating costs should fall in Q3. The 10-Q says consolidation savings begin in Q3 2026 after Q2 opex of $24.9m, which was inflated by acquisition and integration costs. The FY gross-margin guide was raised to 40-45% (Q2 was 44%). The Oct 7 update says most of the Luminar-asset integration, including the Orlando consolidation, is complete and promises a 'significant reduction in cash burn in 2027'. An adj. EBITDA loss and EPS better than Q2's -$1.66 against a -$0.75 consensus is possible; the consensus looks stale against recent actuals.
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: EPS has missed in 5 of 7 quarters. The Q2 EPS miss ($-1.66 vs $-0.75) coincided with +3.99%, so EPS is not the line this stock trades on.
findings.why_not_priced: The cost line sits inside what the company has guided (the ~$60m FY burn), so it is mostly expected. Sized small for that reason.
findings.independence: Q2 release on cash burn normalizing in H2 (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/0000065770/000149315226036350/ex99-1.htm); Oct 7 8-K on integration completion.

findings.finding: On 2026-10-15 Overland AI selected MicroVision's IRIS long-range lidar for its next-generation IBEX autonomous defense ground vehicle. It is a design win with no disclosed value, the latest in a run of defense/industrial IRIS announcements (APAC pilot, defense AGV, Robinson Unmanned).
findings.reaction_history_on_this_line: The stock rose 5% on 2026-10-15 ($1.17 to $1.23) and gave it back the next day ($1.13).
findings.why_not_priced: Mostly priced: it is public and the stock faded it. It counts only if the call quantifies defense volume. The price already shows design wins without dollars do not move the stock.
findings.independence: The 2026-10-07 8-K lists IRIS defense AGV deployments (https://www.sec.gov/Archives/edgar/data/65770/000149315226046140/ex99-1.htm).

outside_window.finding: HALO next-generation customer transitions are expected from late 2027 into 2028, and the MOVIA S launch (October 2026) is a 2027 revenue driver by the company's own statement. Neither lands in Q3 or Q4 revenue.

baseline_tension: There is no skew to agree or disagree with. The findings net slightly positive against a -18% 20-day run-up and a stock already at its 52-week low area, while the name's own reaction history (6 of 7 prints down) and its financing pattern argue negative. So p_up sits below 50 and the per-finding sum sits near zero.
lessons_applied: Lesson 6 (bar has one source, MarketBeat $2.0m, Investing unspecified): reported-quarter revenue finding capped, +1.0 -> +0.7.
Lessons 4 and 7: financing is answered as negative (going concern, covenant, no corroborated ramp), but the ~20% short with 27% borrow shrinks it, -3.0 -> -2.5.
Lesson 1 (Q1 revenue beat sold -21%): already reflected in the small revenue size and in p_up 42; not applied again.
Lesson 8: abs_move_pct kept at 13, above the 11.57 median, for thin turnover and a crowded short; unchanged from the draft.
Guidance, positioning, opex and design-win findings left standing.
